chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted on Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazal, on the authority of Ali ibn Aqabah ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father Aqabah ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abu Abdullah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, peace be upon them.
He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The precinct of the mosque is forty cubits, and the neighborhood is forty houses from its four sides.'
ai.seo_question: What are the defined boundaries of a mosque's precinct and neighborhood in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal delineates the spatial jurisprudence of mosque precincts, defining the sacred boundary (haram) as forty cubits and the associated residential neighborhood (jawar) as forty houses in each direction. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking physical sanctity with community structure, ensuring that the immediate vicinity of the mosque remains protected and conducive to worship. This measurement underscores the importance of maintaining a distinct, reverent environment around the house of God.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 22-20 Al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted on Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hassan, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faz’zal, on the authority of Ali ibn Aqabah ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father Aqabah ibn Khalid, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB) that the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) said, “The neighborhood zone of a mosque is forty ells , and the precincts of a mosque span out to forty houses away in each direction.”
